headline: Judiciary Introduces Mandatory ‘Literalism Test’ for All Insects Entering Courtrooms
body:
Following recent debates regarding the metaphorical versus entomological status of courtroom visitors, the Supreme Court administrative wing has announced a new protocol requiring all household pests to undergo a rigorous linguistic competency screening before entering the premises. The move aims to prevent future misunderstandings by ensuring that any six-legged attendee understands the nuances of legal jurisprudence before attempting to influence judicial proceedings.

“We have installed specialized micro-intercoms at all entrance gates where insects are now asked to clarify if their presence is intended as a literal crawl or a metaphorical rhetorical device,” said Court Registrar A. K. Sharma. “If the creature cannot articulate its stance on contemporary legal ethics in a clear, non-malicious manner, it is politely redirected to the garden outside to continue its activities in a strictly private capacity.”

Legal experts note that the new policy will include a mandatory orientation session for local populations of cockroaches, houseflies, and silverfish. The orientation focuses on the distinction between being a ‘disturbing presence’ and a ‘dramatic linguistic metaphor,’ with certificates of compliance provided to those who can successfully navigate the complexities of constitutional interpretation without scurrying across the bar table during a hearing.
caption: Law is not for the faint of heart, or for bugs who don’t understand irony. The courts are officially establishing boundaries. #Law #Judiciary #LegalHumor #TafriTimes (satire)
